comments.body:
## Additional evidence: the failing tests LEAK orphaned processes at PPID 1

Measured immediately after the `make verify` run that produced the 22 failures (2026-10-27 ~23:58 PDT).

`ps -Ao pid,ppid,etime,command` found **32 surviving `bash .../infra/scripts/observability.sh` processes** — 16 parents, each at **PPID 1**, each with one child. Their elapsed times ran from 8 m 19 s to 21 m 41 s, i.e. they had been accumulating steadily through the test run and outlived it.

```
646     1  16:33  bash .../infra/scripts/observability.sh
647   646  16:33  bash .../infra/scripts/observability.sh
6372    1  15:32  ...
...                      (16 PPID-1 parents in total)
72536   1  21:41  ...
```

I reaped all 32 by explicit PID; none remain.

### Why this happens, and why it compounds the bug

`_run` invokes the script with `subprocess.run(["bash", str(SCRIPT)], env=env, timeout=60)`. On `TimeoutExpired` Python kills the **direct** child only. The script has already forked its own subshell, which survives, reparents to `init`, and keeps running — unbounded, since nothing else holds a reference to it.

So each failing case leaves a process behind. With the `/var/lib/rebar` writes failing, every affected case times out, and the run leaks one orphan pair per timeout. On a developer host running repeated verifies these accumulate without limit; AGENTS.md treats a process reaching PPID 1 as the documented orphan class (`docs/orphaned-processes.md`), and `python3 scripts/check_orphaned_load.py` is the detector for exactly this.

### Effect on the acceptance criteria

Fixing the `/var/lib/rebar` override gap removes the timeouts and therefore the leak in practice, but it does not fix the leak itself: any future timeout in these tests will orphan again. Add to the plan:

- `_run` must reap the whole process group on timeout, not just the direct child — start the script in its own session/process group and signal that group on `TimeoutExpired`, then `wait` on it.
- Add an assertion, or a fixture teardown check, that no `observability.sh` process survives the test — so a reintroduced leak fails the suite instead of accumulating silently on the host.

Suggested additional acceptance criterion:

- [ ] After the four observability test files run (including an induced timeout), no `infra/scripts/observability.sh` process survives and none reaches PPID 1.

## Reproduction on arm64 macOS, 2026-10-31 (worktree at origin/main 0886e96f03a)

**The 4 files pass on an unmodified tree here:** `29 passed in 268.42s` (`-n 4`). No commit since 2026-10-27 touches `infra/scripts/observability.sh` or these 4 files, so main has not fixed this; the failure is load-dependent.

**The missing `/var/lib/rebar` paths do not cause the timeout.** Every write to them is `... 2>/dev/null || true`. The two stderr lines in the description come from bash reporting the failed `>` redirect before `2>/dev/null` applies; the script continues and exits 0. The 29 passes above ran with `/var/lib/rebar` absent and those same lines on stderr.

**What makes a run slow: the tests reach the host's real Docker daemon, with no time limit.**
- `mcp_health_9ea3`, `offsets_6a65`, `marker_anchor_8c2f`, `mcp_markers` stub `curl`, `git`, `logger`, `journalctl`, `aws`, but not `docker`. Inside the test environment, `docker` resolves to `/opt/homebrew/bin/docker` (colima): `docker system df` took 6 s, `docker stats --no-stream` 3 s.
- This host has no `timeout`/`gtimeout`, so the script's `bounded()` falls back to running each probe with no limit (documented intent at the definition, for portable test hosts).
- One script run: 15.9 s and 16.9 s with real docker; 5.5 s and 5.0 s with `docker` stubbed to `exit 1`. Load average at the time was about 40 on 18 cores.

**Controlled reproduction of the reported failure:** a `docker` stub that runs `exec sleep 75`, driven through the unmodified `_run` from `mcp_health_9ea3`, raised `TimeoutExpired` at 60.0 s with exactly the 2 stderr lines in the description, and left `bash observability.sh` at PPID 1 with its child and the `sleep` (reaped by pid). This shows that a stalled host probe alone yields the reported signature and the orphan leak in the earlier comment. Whether colima was the stalled probe in the 2026-10-27 run has not been measured.

**Isolation gaps are suite-wide, not limited to these 4 files.** The script has 16 `NAME="${NAME:-/var/lib/rebar/...}"` defaults. Every one of the 21 test files that drives `observability.sh` leaves between 4 and 16 of them unset; only 7 of the 21 stub `docker`. The 4 named files leave 10, 10, 8 and 5 unset respectively. Reads also reach `/var/tmp`, `/var/lib/docker`, `/var/log/journal`, `/var/gerrit`, `/etc/...` and `/usr/local/bin/rebar-*-cap.sh`.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation

A `make verify` on arm64 macOS (2026-10-27) failed 22 tests plus 1 error, all in 4 files that drive `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (`test_observability_mcp_health_9ea3.py`, `_offsets_6a65.py`, `_marker_anchor_8c2f.py`, `_mcp_markers.py`). Each failing case raised `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` after the tests' 60 s bound; stderr also named `/var/lib/rebar/probe-region` and `/var/lib/rebar/reviewbot-webhook-auth-offset` as missing. Reproduction evidence is in the comments.

## Root cause

1. **The tests reach the host's real Docker daemon with no bound.** The script calls `docker system df`, `docker ps` and `docker stats --no-stream` through `clamped`/`bounded`. On a host without coreutils `timeout` (stock macOS), `bounded` deliberately runs the command unbounded. 12 of the 19 test files that run the whole script do not stub `docker`, so each run waits on the host daemon: measured 6 s (`system df`) + 3 s (`stats`) per run on colima, 16–17 s per script run versus 5 s with `docker` stubbed. Under load this exceeds 60 s; a `docker` stub that stalls reproduces the exact `TimeoutExpired` signature.
2. **Timeouts orphan the script.** `subprocess.run(..., timeout=...)` kills only the direct `bash`; the script's subshells and their children survive at PPID 1 (16 orphaned pairs measured after the 2026-10-27 run; reproduced here).
3. **No test redirects every host state path.** The script defaults 17 state paths (lines 33, 34, 67, 77, 920, 952, 971, 992, 1013–1018, 1021, 1022, 1076) to `/var/lib/rebar/...` (`NAME="${NAME:-/var/lib/rebar/...}"`). Every one of the 19 files leaves between 4 and 15 of the 17 unset, so runs try to read and write the real host directory. On this host the writes fail silently (`2>/dev/null || true`), so this is not what times out — but a host where `/var/lib/rebar` exists (the production layout) would have test runs read and overwrite real offset state, and nothing stops a new path being added unredirected.

The missing-path stderr lines are a symptom, not the cause of the timeout: the script continues and exits 0.

## Approach (test-side; production defaults unchanged)

Scope: all 19 files under `tests/scripts/test_observability_*.py` that run the whole script. The other 2 (`_cap_deps`, `_pct_of_cap_b380`) only read the script text or run one extracted function, and are left as they are.

1. Add one shared helper module `tests/_observability_harness.py` (beside `tests/_subprocess_env.py`, so a nested pytest that loads a test module as a plugin can import it; `test_observability_exit.py` gets the same explicit `tests/` sys.path bootstrap `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` uses for that case). It passes the redacted `SubprocessEnv` through without unwrapping it:
   - `state_path_defaults()` parses the script for every `NAME="${NAME:-/var/lib/rebar/...}"` default (17 today; the number is derived from the script, never hard-coded), so a path added to the script is redirected without editing any test.
   - `INSTANCE_ID_CACHE` (line 73) has no literal default: it derives from the directory of `REGION_CACHE`, so redirecting `REGION_CACHE` redirects it. The helper also sets it explicitly to the same `tmp_path` directory so the redirect does not depend on that derivation.
   - `observability_env(tmp_path)` returns the subprocess environment with every such variable pointing into `tmp_path`, and a fallback `docker` stub (`exit 1`, i.e. unavailable) placed ahead of the host `PATH`. A test's own `bin/` stubs are prepended after it, so tests that stub `docker` keep their stub. Test-specific overrides still win because tests update the env afterwards.
   - `run_observability(argv, env=..., timeout=...)` starts the script in its own session and, on timeout, kills the whole process group and reaps it before re-raising `TimeoutExpired`. Before starting, it refuses (AssertionError naming the variable and its default) any env in which a state variable still resolves under `/var/lib/rebar`, or whose `docker` is the host's binary, so an unredirected path fails fast in under a second instead of timing out.
2. Convert the 19 files to build their env with `observability_env` and run the script with `run_observability`. No assertion, stub or scenario changes; existing per-file timeouts (60/120/180/300 s) are kept.
3. Add the guard test `tests/scripts/test_observability_harness_isolation.py`:
   - every non-comment `/var/lib/rebar` literal in the script sits in a parsed `${NAME:-...}` default (a hard-coded path fails and names its line);
   - the number of parsed defaults equals the number of non-comment lines naming `/var/lib/rebar`, and includes the 17 names present today (anti-vacuity for the parser);
   - `INSTANCE_ID_CACHE` is set under `tmp_path` by `observability_env`, and the script still derives it from `REGION_CACHE`'s directory (if that derivation changes, the test names it);
   - no test file in `tests/scripts/` runs `observability.sh` (or a copy) through `subprocess` directly — every whole-script run goes through `run_observability` (AST scan; names file and line);
   - `run_observability` rejects an env missing one state variable, naming it;
   - an induced timeout (stub that sleeps) leaves no surviving `observability.sh` process.
4. Do not change `infra/scripts/observability.sh`, raise the 60 s bound, skip, or mark any test platform-specific.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every one of the script's `/var/lib/rebar` defaults (17 today) is set under `tmp_path` by `observability_env`, verified by `test_observability_env_redirects_every_state_path`.
- [ ] `run_observability` refuses an env that leaves any state variable under `/var/lib/rebar`, naming the variable, in under 5 s; verified by a guard test that deletes `REGION_CACHE`.
- [ ] A non-comment `/var/lib/rebar` literal outside a `NAME="${NAME:-...}"` default fails the guard test, which names its line.
- [ ] No test in `tests/scripts/` runs `observability.sh` (or a copy) through `subprocess` directly; the AST guard names any file and line that does, and its anti-vacuity case proves it detects one.
- [ ] `run_observability` refuses, naming the path, an env whose `PATH` resolves `docker` to the same binary the ambient `PATH` resolves; a guard test proves the refusal, so every whole-script run uses the fallback stub or the test's own.
- [ ] After an induced timeout, the stalled probe's grandchild process is gone within 10 s.
- [ ] `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_*.py` passes on arm64 macOS with no manual host setup.
- [ ] `/var/lib/rebar` does not exist on this host after that run.
- [ ] `pytest tests/scripts/` passes.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] `git diff origin/main -- infra/scripts/observability.sh` is empty.
- [ ] No test is skipped or marked platform-specific by this change.
- [ ] Per-run script time with real docker versus the stub is recorded on this ticket, before and after the change.

Not in scope: bug `degraded-chilly-galago` (pandoc on arm64), which is the other blocker for a green `make verify` on arm64 macOS.
